items.reason: Header precedes the status table and names the set, resolved Runtime path, and binding kind.
Whole-set setup prints the header regardless of invocation checkout.
Invocation from a Runtime subdirectory omits “invoked from” because comparison normalizes cwd to the checkout root.
Routing’s BoundDefault flag triggers the binding-recorded announcement.
The old “draining at bound checkout” output is removed.
AFK task-file execution prints the current-checkout path without a Drain header.
HITL execution returns through runTargetedHITLGate before reaching the new current-checkout line.
Successful whole-set execution prints one green “✓ <set>/<task> done” line.
Commit SHA or verified no-op detail prints directly beneath the success line.
The old completion printer is removed, and each task ending has one result-printing branch.
Exhausted retries that fail the task produce one red failed result line.
Provider exhaustion preserves the open task and prints one red “out of agents (left open)” result.
Quota parking prints the yellow quota-paused line with the selected preset.
Interrupted execution maps to the yellow interrupted result line.
Blocked and Deferred remain set-level reports; executed tasks retain their individual result lines.
Attempt-failure narration, timing breakdowns, and exhausted-walk narration remain intact.
Both new printers use the existing output wrapper, preserving complete plain text for redirected output.
Result styles use existing terminal color detection and NO_COLOR suppression.
Header and result printing introduce no journal writes.

scores.rationale: Clear, centralized output handling with useful regression tests, but missing HITL and subdirectory coverage leaves two required behaviors incorrect.
